call_accounting.scope: the tests in this file. Every payload is a line of the committed capture or a mutation of one, and both transports are local structs with counters, so nothing here opens a socket. The read-shape guards added beside the production code live elsewhere and are counted in the §11 inventory: two unit tests in crates/live/src/preconf_provider.rs run on stubs, and one test in crates/chain/tests/readiness_gate.rs sends two requests to a 127.0.0.1 stub that records the params it was sent.

transport.detail: these three are the atomic counters of the local stubs in `the_radar_asks_for_the_shape_its_decoder_reads`, which asserts the table and the live counters agree; a stub that silently read twice would make this file disagree with its own run

frame_facts.wire_index_detail: the pending payload has no frame index field of any kind (measured field set: the standard block object)

cases.input: the first captured pending answer, unmodified
cases.note: the shape M9.4 characterised and the shape §6 keeps: every transaction entry is an object, so every target is nameable.

cases.error_line: payload transaction is not a full object (hash-only list), so the radar cannot name its target
cases.input: the same captured block with each transaction replaced by its own hash
cases.note: this is what `pending_raw` returns; the radar refuses it rather than reporting an empty affected-pool set that would read as a quiet market.

cases.error_line: payload field `transactions[].hash` is missing or not a hex quantity; fail-closed
cases.input: the captured block with transactions[0].hash removed
cases.note: a frame is identified by its transactions; without a hash there is nothing to reconcile against the sealed block.

cases.error_line: payload field `number` is missing or not a hex quantity; fail-closed
cases.input: the captured block with its `number` removed
cases.note: height is the one field a pending view cannot be held without; there is no fallback to a local counter.

cases.error_line: pending transactions[1] is a number, which is neither a full transaction object nor a bare hash; fail-closed
cases.input: the captured block with transactions[1] replaced by 42
cases.note: not a hash list and not an object; the refusal names the index and the kind it found.

cases.error_line: pending transactions[2] is a array, which is neither a full transaction object nor a bare hash; fail-closed
cases.input: the captured block with transactions[2] replaced by a one-element array
cases.note: a nested list would have decoded as "hash-only" under the previous wording, which pointed at a read parameter the payload never used.

cases.case: transaction entry is a truncated hash
cases.error_line: pending transactions[3] is a string, which is neither a full transaction object nor a bare hash; fail-closed
cases.input: the captured block with transactions[3] replaced by a 4-byte hex string
cases.note: the near-miss: a string that is not 32 bytes is not a bare hash, and is not reported as one.

cases.error_line: payload field `transactions` is missing or not a hex quantity; fail-closed
cases.input: the captured block whose `transactions` is a map instead of a list
cases.note: the array itself is required; a map is not "the same thing in another shape".

frame_facts.wire_index_detail: the pending payload has no frame index field of any kind (measured field set: the standard block object)

cases.input: the captured block plus a key the decoder does not read
cases.note: an unmapped key cannot create a claim: every field the frame carries is read by name, so the frame is the one the unmodified payload produced.

frame_facts.wire_index_detail: the payload names an index-like key (`index` or `sequence`) that this decoder does not map, so the frame index stays local (§8)

cases.input: the same payload plus an `index` key
cases.note: kept unknown and recorded as present: §8 assigns the frame index from read order, and the detail line now says the key was named but not mapped instead of claiming no such field exists.

decision.chosen: change the request params on the radar's own read
decision.latency: NOT_MEASURED: this milestone reads no real node, and a larger response on the same method cannot be claimed cheaper without a sample
decision.why_not_the_decoder: a hash list names no contract, so accepting one would turn an empty affected-pool set into a finding; §6.5 forbids relaxing validation to make an unknown shape pass
decision.why_not_the_shared_read: the candidate observer's fact is a count of transactions, not their targets, so it would pay the full-object byte multiple measured in size_stats for bytes it never opens; see full_over_bare_hundredths

negative_controls.planted: PollingFrameSource::next_view asks HeadReader::pending_raw instead of pending_full_transactions
the wrong-type refusal collapsed back into HashOnlyTransaction, as it was before §6
an index-like key reported as no frame index field of any kind

negative_controls.note: the only guard for this one is the wire test: every other test in §6 sits above a stub that implements both pending methods, so the flag could regress here and stay green there
